verdicts.explanation: The paper reports the Nernst-Einstein conductivity of Li3PS4 glass as 19.7 × 10−3 S cm−1, derived from an Arrhenius extrapolation to 300 K. Origin (computational), temperature (300 K = 26.85 °C), and the null secondary fields all match the paper, and no activation energy is stated explicitly.
The paper cites a value of 19.0 × 10−3 S cm−1 from prior simulations (ref. 14) for Li3PS4 glass, so literature_cited is correct. No measurement temperature is given, so null is correct.

The paper quotes experimental Li3PS4 glass conductivity of ∼2.8–3.0 × 10−4 S cm−1 from refs. 11 and 15, which matches the record as literature_cited. The paper gives no measurement temperature, so null is correct.
